notes: Summary: Embercrest is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for low-latency inference of a trading chat assistant + reranker. Primary focus is making p95/p99 SLOs predictable under bursty market conditions and agreeing reserved GPU counts for guaranteed throughput.

Key ask from Embercrest: a clear, auditable definition of latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) that maps to both streaming and non-streaming traffic, plus alignment on measurement surface (client-side vs server-side).
Their ops lead quote from 2026-03-02: "We need the SLOs to match what our users actually see — not just server-side tail numbers. If the client SDK adds 50-100ms, that changes the SLA math."
Technical constraints: must run inside customer VPC for market data residency. On-prem proof-of-concept for DR site (air-gapped option discussed). Key management via customer KMS required.

Latency targets discussed: non-streaming (batch inference) goal = p95 <= 150ms, p99 <= 300ms under steady-state production; streaming (chat) goal = time-to-first-byte p95 <= 120ms, end-to-stream p95 <= 350ms. Embercrest expects p99 streaming tail < 600ms but understands need for negotiated fallbacks.
Measurement plan proposed by SE (Jordan Liu):
- Define measurement surfaces: client-end-to-last-byte (user-visible), gateway-to-last-byte (edge measured), and server-processing-only (runtime internal) — capture all three in benchmarks.
- Synthetic benchmarks: run 72-hour stepped load test with 1M synthetic requests/day to observe p50/p95/p99, and correlated GPU utilization for each model and seq-length distribution.
- Shadow testing: 2-week shadow of 10% real traffic into Dedicated pool to validate real-workload tails and KV cache hit distributions.

- Streaming measurement specifics: instrument TTFB and per-token inter-arrival times; measure time-to-first-token and time-to-last-token separately. Use Firefly call timestamps and SDK traces to correlate client vs server timing.

Discussed fallbacks and graceful degradation: pre-negotiated fallback to smaller model family or lower token budget when Dedicated pool is saturated; Redwood to provide automatic routing policy and a clear metric that counts 'fallback' events for SLA crediting.

Throughput & reserved GPU planning notes: Embercrest wants a capacity plan showing GPU counts for baseline (95th percentile load) and peak (99th percentile) with autoscale buffer. Initial ask: guidance for 8x A100-class GPUs for low-latency single-guest models, with burst pool of 2 GPUs. SE to provide model-by-model throughput matrix.
Security & compliance progress: security questionnaire 80% complete, SOC2 attestation acceptable, customer KMS integration pilot scheduled 2026-03-18, audit-log schema reviewed 2026-03-05.

Commercial / SLA negotiation points: Embercrest requests credits for any p99 exceedance measured at the client surface; Redwood proposes measuring server-side p99 with an agreed add-on delta for SDK overhead. Legal to reconcile during procurement.

- 2026-03-12: deliver synthetic benchmark report + GPU sizing recommendation (SE deliverable)
- 2026-03-18: KMS integration smoke test in VPC POC

- Legal: provide redline of SLA where client-side measurement counts toward credits; recommend middle-ground: server-measured p99 + SDK telemetry delta allowance.
